| description = '''Respawn timer of 18 hours, with a +/- 1 hour variance.'''[https://web.archive.org/web/20100226064508/http://everquest.allakhazam.com/wiki/EQ:Respawn_Timers] Ability to ''skip'' spawn cycles. Located at (5823, 728). The spawn is considered a "camp" and not a first-to-engage outdoor mob.[https://www.project1999.com/forums/showthread.php?t=211886]

'''<b>NOTE 6/1/22:</b>''' ''If the server repops for any reason <B>other than a Quake</B> (anything that takes you out of the game world), the list no longer applies. Stormfeather and Lodizal will always be up instantly and will <b>always</b> be FTE, even if there was a list there for 100 hours. Effectively, if Stormfeather spawns from anything other than natural camped 17-19 spawns <b>or</b> Quake, it is FTE (outside of quakes). Due to the bird being one-shottable by Sunstrike or even a Trakanon Tooth, this does raise some questions, like why it had it's yellow FTE message removed, or how people expect to get on the aggro list when many classes can literally instantly kill it (Necro/Wiz/Mage wands, anyone with Trak Tooth, Harm Touch, etc. These situations will need to be petitioned.''[https://www.project1999.com/forums/showthread.php?t=249060]

'''<b>Notes about camping:</b>''' ''Beware, as he will begin wandering away almost immediately after spawning if not engaged. There are many rumors out there regarding his spawn patterns, but all my observations have supported the 18 hour +/- 1 hour rule. He has been known to skip up to 3 times. Note that when he skips a respawn, the new 18 hour +/- 1 window starts from a completely random time within the original window. This effectively extends his new window by 1 hour in either direction, so that the pattern becomes 1st window: 18 +/- 1, 2nd window: 36 +/- 2, 3rd window: 54 +/- 3. It's also worth being aware that while the probability of him spawning is completely uniform within the 2 hour window of the first spawn, once he skips, he is more likely to spawn in the middle of the window than towards the ends. This is similar to rolling dice: 1 6-sided die has an equal chance to produce any number between 1 and 6; 2 6-sided dice are more likely to produce a result around 7, while 2 and 12 are relatively rare, and so on.''
